The speaking likeness was a genre of the figure in Renaissance sculpture and painting that sought to capture momentary, ephemeral motions or expressions, particularly subtle details indicative of a subject speaking or preparing to speak. The style was popularized by the biographic work of Italian artist Gian Lorenzo Bernini. It is an extreme form of naturalism that arose in a period where human subjects were typically instead deified as untouchable, larger-than-life figures.
